title: A Love Left Unspoken
content:
Yashwanth lowered his gaze.

For a few moments...

He remained silent, as though searching for the courage to relive memories that still hurt.

Finally, he looked at Siddu.

"Do you remember Varsha?"

"Our classmate from Hyderabad."

Siddu thought for a moment before nodding.

"Yes."

"I remember her."

A faint smile appeared on Yashwanth's face.

"During college..."

"Varsha and I were very close."

"We spent almost every day together."

"We laughed together..."

"Studied together..."

"And slowly..."

"Our friendship became something neither of us could explain."

"We never knew whether it was just friendship..."

"Or something more."

After graduation, both of us got busy with our careers.

I moved to Shimla after getting my job, while she went her own way.

Even then...

We never completely lost touch.

We spoke once in a while, asking about work and life.

Life seemed ordinary...

Until one unexpected morning.

"My manager called me into his cabin."

"He said a new employee named Varsha would be joining our team."

Yashwanth smiled softly.

"I was confused."

"I wondered..."

"Could it really be our Varsha?"

A few minutes later...

The cabin door opened.

She walked in.

The moment our eyes met...

Time seemed to stand still.

"It really was her."

Neither of us had expected fate to bring us back together like that.

Working in the same office brought us even closer.

We had lunch together...

Worked on projects together...

Stayed back after office discussing everything from work to our dreams.

Every passing day...

Our bond grew deeper.

Without realizing it...

She had become the most important part of my life.

Then...

My birthday arrived.

A gentle smile appeared on Yashwanth's face as the memory unfolded.

"That day..."

"She wore a beautiful red-and-black saree."

"The moment I saw her..."

"I couldn't take my eyes off her."

"It wasn't just the saree..."

"It was the smile on her face."

"She looked..."

"Like an angel."

Siddu quietly smiled, listening to his friend.

"She stayed by my side almost the entire day."

"In the evening, I threw a small party for my teammates."

Everyone eventually left.

Except Varsha.

She stayed back.

The two of us stood quietly outside the office, enjoying the cool evening breeze.

I smiled at her.

"Thank you."

"You made my birthday really special."

She didn't reply.

She simply lowered her eyes.

For a moment...

I thought I had said something wrong.

Then...

Without warning...

She slowly stepped closer.

Before I could understand what was happening...

She gently kissed my cheek.

My heartbeat completely lost its rhythm.

Yashwanth smiled sadly.

"I was completely shocked."

She immediately took a step back.

Her cheeks had turned bright red.

She nervously held my hand.

Then, gathering every bit of courage she had...

She looked into my eyes.

"I love you, Yashwanth."

"I've loved you since our college days."

"I just never had the courage to tell you."

"But today..."

"I couldn't hold it back anymore."

Tears shimmered in her eyes, yet she smiled through her nervousness.

Then, before I could even respond...

She ran away.

Yashwanth let out a quiet laugh.

"It felt unreal."

"I couldn't stop smiling."

"I had already decided."

"I was going to say yes."

"But before giving her my answer..."

"I wanted to tell my parents first."

"I wanted their blessings."

Siddu smiled.

"That sounds exactly like you."

Yashwanth's smile slowly faded.

"I reached home that night..."

"My heart was lighter than it had ever been."

"I was excited to tell my parents everything."

He lowered his eyes once again.

"But before I could say a single word..."

"My father spoke first."

"He smiled at me and said..."

"'We've fixed your marriage.'"

Yashwanth's voice trembled.

"With..."

"My friend's daughter."

"I just stood there."

"I couldn't speak."

"I wanted to tell them..."

"I really did."

"But the words refused to leave my mouth."

"All I could do..."

"Was stand there in silence."

"Watching the happiest day of my life..."

"Turn into the most painful one."

The room fell silent.

Siddu looked at his friend without saying a word.

For the first time...

He truly understood why Yashwanth's voice had sounded so broken over the phone.

And deep inside...

He knew this was only the beginning of a story that carried far more pain than he had imagined.
